in_arabic.name: سابق

in_urdu.name: سابق
in_urdu.meaning: سابق کا مطلب ہے جو سب سے پہلے کسی کام کو کرتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: سابق (Saabiq) کا نام عربی زبان سے نکلا ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے 'پہلا' یا 'جو سب سے پہلے کسی کام کو کرتا ہے'۔ یہ نام اسلامی تقویم میں بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے، خاص طور پر رمضان کے مہینے میں جب پہلے روزہ دار سب سے پہلے روزہ رکھتے ہیں۔

in_hindi.name: साबिक
in_hindi.meaning: साबिक का अर्थ है जो सबसे पहले किसी काम को करता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: साबिक (Saabiq) नाम का अर्थ है 'पहला' या 'अग्रणी'। यह नाम उन लोगों के लिए चुना जाता है जो अपने कार्यों में सबसे पहले होते हैं और दूसरों का नेतृत्व करते हैं। इस नाम का चयन करने वाले माता-पिता अपने बच्चे के लिए एक अद्वितीय और अर्थपूर्ण नाम ढूंढते हैं।

The name is mentioned in the Quran, emphasizing the importance of being the first to engage in righteous actions.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Saabiq" in Islamic culture is used to refer to a person or group that goes before others in various aspects of life. It can refer to a leader who goes before his people, a scholar who goes before others in knowledge, or a prominent figure who paves the way for new ideas or movements. The significance of being a Saabiq is often associated with courage, wisdom, and the ability to set new trends and break new grounds.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual realm, being a Saabiq is a virtue that is highly valued in Islamic tradition. It is a reminder that every believer should strive to be a forerunner in following the guidance of Allah, as outlined in the Quran and the Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Being a Saabiq in one's faith means being diligent in practicing Islam and continually seeking knowledge to deepen one's understanding of the religion. It also means being a role model and mentor to others, guiding them towards the right path and setting an excellent example for them to follow. Ultimately, being a Saabiq is a way to draw closer to Allah and to serve as a means of His pleasure.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Sa'd, Al-Tabaqat Al-Kubra, vol.3, p.113 - 115 The name Saabiq carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Sa'd provides biographies of early Islamic scholars and their students. Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd Al-Khudri, known as Ibrahim Al-Sa'biq (The Pioneer), was an early student of Imam Malik ibn Anas, and one of the first scholars to transmit Maliki law from its founder.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Dhahabi, Siyar A'lam An-Nubala, vol.3, p.300 - 302 The name Saabiq carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Al-Dhahabi describes Ibrahim Al-Sa'biq as a renowned scholar and teacher in the Maliki legal tradition, who studied under Imam Malik ibn Anas and his chief student, Said ibn Al-Musayyab. He was one of the first scholars to transmit Maliki law to other regions outside of Medina.
